title: Rotation and Recovery
summary: Recovered a 128-bit key from a stateful protocol using an adversary-in-the-middle seat, a verification oracle, and a factorable key schedule, then cut the edit cost with a two-stage residue lift.

title: Deanonymizing a Wi-Fi Device from a Probe-Request Capture
summary: Found the one device in a 39,000-device Wi-Fi probe capture that never randomized its MAC, then read its leaked saved-network list back as a travel itinerary. The whole solve turned on a single bit.

title: Four Merits and a Final Petition
summary: A courtly LLM refused my direct and acrostic requests. I earned four merits, corrected a final petition, and submitted the disclosed flag successfully. The case becomes a proposed gateway and purple team test.

title: Three Code Objects in One Python Function
summary: A Python flag checker kept replacing one function's code object. I matched its bytecode to the right interpreter, read the RC4 check, and reversed it to recover the accepted input.

title: The Calculator That Waited for an ICMP Echo
summary: A stripped calculator contained a passive raw-ICMP receive loop. I read its packet checks and identified the crafted Echo Request that activated a reverse-shell callback.

title: Fifteen Videos, One Hidden PDF
summary: Fifteen playable MP4 files each carried a short PDF fragment in a trailing uuid box. I used PDF structure and zlib validation to restore the document despite misleading filenames.

title: The Calculator That Renamed Itself
summary: A trojanized calculator detached from its terminal and overwrote its own command line with a familiar service name. I traced that rename in a stripped ELF without running its backdoor.

title: When the Answer File Stopped Carrying Information
summary: I read a Haskell compile-time transform, inverted its answer forms, and found the point where its state became zero and the transcript stopped revealing the key.

title: The Click Between Two Meows
summary: A stereo cat recording hid a brief one-channel burst. I read its sample amplitudes as Morse-like timing after the spectrogram and bit-plane checks came up empty.

title: The Flag That Read Backward
summary: A series hint pointed toward XOR, but this first token kept the shape of a flag. I tried Atbash, checked the reversible mapping, and submitted the recovered answer.
